title: Would it be risky to make and share a free, non-commercial Chiikawa fan game?
author: TonyMaow
selftext:
Hi! I have a bit of a dilemma. To give you a quick summary:

I want to create a personal project: a co-op Chiikawa RPG. I saw that Chiikawa Adventures had been taken down in Roblox, and I've wanted to work on a personal, non-commercial project just for fun for quite some time, so I saw this as an opportunity. I'm an illustrator, and I'm really drawn to the creative and visual side of things. I'm not particularly fond of programming, but I have no problem learning along the way, and I'm not in any rush.

The thing is, I initially envisioned this as something just for my boyfriend and me to play, but the Chiikawa community is very active, and I think a lot of people would enjoy the project as well. My idea would be to distribute it anonymously, completely free of charge, and potentially accept entirely voluntary donations. These would simply be optional contributions as a way of showing appreciation, with absolutely no rewards or benefits in return.

I would create all the artwork myself. I'd mainly rely on AI to help me learn programming, speed up the workflow, and perhaps make certain creative processes more efficient. I might also use AI for some audio assets, although that part is still undecided.

My biggest concern is copyright. Initially, I plan to distribute the game very discreetly, sharing it anonymously through Facebook groups and allowing people to redistribute it freely. I might also set up a Discord server where people could follow the project's progress and participate in polls. I've even considered making it Spanish-only to limit its reach a little further (I'm from Colombia, and Spanish is my native language).

As for the copyright issue, obviously, the game would be based on Chiikawa's story, universe, and characters (although the playable characters would be OCs). I'd also probably draw inspiration from quite a few elements of Chiikawa Pocket, such as its icons, weapons, etc.

I know I'd technically be infringing on copyright, since I don't own the rights to any of this material, even if the project is non-commercial. And I'm definitely not planning to obtain a license or anything like that lol.

It's simply something I want to make out of pure enjoyment.

**What kind of reach do you think would be reasonable for a project like this?**

I was planning to announce the project itself on a few social media platforms using completely new accounts created specifically for this purpose. But honestly, I don't want to put years of work into something only to have it taken down after all that effort, especially when my only intention is to make the fandom happy.

I have no problem keeping it 100% personal if that's the safest option, but it would make me a little sad not to be able to share it with the Chiikawa community.

fan project.

comments.author: crackedpotstudio

So you want to basically rip off an artist work and make money from it? (Why are you taking donations otherwise?)

People like you are the reason AI in game development is so hated right now…

replies.author: TonyMaow
replies.body:
What the hell—no! I said I was considering accepting donations because, while it’s based on \*Chiikawa\*, I’d be doing all the illustration work myself—and creating a video game takes a \*lot\* of time. It’s a project that would likely take me two years just to release a demo.

Actually, I’m open to the suggestion of \*not\* accepting donations if you think that’s the better approach. I have no financial interest in this project; in fact, I don’t want to put that kind of pressure on myself, as I’m doing this purely for fun—to learn and enjoy the process. Besides, the original plan was just to make it so my boyfriend and I could play it. I’m just a huge fan of \*Chiikawa\* and RPGs—I have absolutely no ill intentions. That’s precisely why I brought up the topic of donations—to get some advice—but your approach to the subject was incredibly aggressive. What the hell?

Edit (I wanted to clarify the above as soon as possible): I was \*considering\* the idea of ​​accepting donations, as it’s a common gesture of appreciation—especially since, as I mentioned, this is a project I’m undertaking entirely on my own. I don’t think it’s unreasonable to imagine that people might want to contribute financially to a project that is distributed for free and took a significant amount of time to create. However—and this is the reason for my post—I’m not entirely clear on the ethical nuances, not just regarding donations, but even concerning the distribution of the game itself, regardless of whether or not I accept any contributions. I genuinely don’t understand how this wasn’t clear. I simply want to create a fan game and see how feasible it is to share it with the community. I have no issue at all with ruling out donations entirely; it was just—and I repeat this because I was taken aback that you even blame me for the hate directed at this community—a possibility I was weighing. I’m not well-versed in many of these matters; I apologize.

comments.author: TonyMaow
comments.body:
But it's not that I want to be financially compensated for my efforts. What I mean is that if people wanted to give me money as a token of appreciation, I wouldn't be opposed to accepting it, obviously. I meant it as a nice gesture, not something I'm actively seeking or wanting. Does that make sense? I don't know if it's a language barrier, but at least to me, there's a clear distinction between the two.

What I want to distinguish, though, are the intentions behind it: I have no intention of monetizing the game itself. I don't want people to give me money so that I can keep developing it, or because I'm supposedly the creator of the Chiikawa universe (because, clearly, I'm not some secret second account of Nagano). I considered the possibility of accepting donations because people tend to offer them for projects like this. They might genuinely want to experience something like what I'm trying to create, and if I had never made and shared it, they would never have had the opportunity to do so.

It's similar to how people make fan art of all kinds of franchises and receive donations simply because they're creating artwork that makes their fans happy. I don't see people constantly going after them or giving them hate for that. I don't think there's anything wrong with someone drawing Chiikawa and sharing it online for me to enjoy, and then having some people send them money because they like their work. So why would it be wrong when it comes to a video game? This is a moral question, not a legal one.

I'll make my project regardless of whether I receive donations. What I wanted was to understand whether accepting donations would be legally and morally acceptable, and likewise, whether distributing the game for free would be acceptable.

It's not because I'm expecting to receive donations in the first place. I just want to know how I would handle the hypothetical situation if someone offered me one, and what reasons or arguments I could give if someone questioned my decision, whether I chose to accept or decline it.

comments.author: TonyMaow
comments.body:
Additionally, no, I don't want to make something similar. I want to make something based on the Chiikawa universe, with its actual characters, because the main purpose is to play it with my partner. I simply want to know whether it would be wise to share it with other people, since Chiikawa has an extremely active community that absolutely loves the characters, the art style, and the universe, and I think they would enjoy the game.

I'm not making something that I initially wanted to share and then happened to decide to base on Chiikawa. I want to make something about Chiikawa specifically so that my boyfriend and I can enjoy it together, and I'm wondering whether, simply because I'd also like to make other people happy, sharing the game could be an option.

I know that in this scenario, if the game is well received, people will offer donations. That's why I brought up the subject in my original post. In the hypothetical scenario where distributing it was legally permissible (I've since looked into it and already found out that it isn't, lol), I needed to understand whether accepting donations would mean, under legal definitions, that the game was no longer free, even if donations were entirely optional and came with absolutely no rewards or benefits. I also wanted to know whether accepting them would somehow be morally wrong.

From what I'm seeing, some people do think so, although I feel like they're simply projecting malicious intentions onto something that's actually quite harmless. But oh well.

comments.author: TonyMaow
comments.body:
The main question wasn't whether I can make a game that accepts donations while distributing it for free.

Those are two separate questions.

Can I make a completely free Chiikawa fangame and distribute it for free?

A separate question, although related to the previous one:

If I were legally allowed to distribute the game for free, would accepting donations change its legal nature?

Because the problem, according to what I've read and researched (not by consulting lawyers, but by reading my country's copyright laws and some international copyright-related regulations), is that I could only make a private-use creation. Even if the game were free, distributing it could still expose me to legal action because, although I would be making the game myself, the Chiikawa universe, its story, and its characters don't belong to me. Distributing the game would mean it was no longer private use of the original work, even if it were completely free.

From a legal standpoint, I could presumably receive donations by making it clear that they aren't payments for the game, but rather contributions to me as a developer or illustrator, without providing donation links or promoting donations in posts or on websites specifically related to that game.

However, if this would generally make people assume that I'm maliciously exploiting the Chiikawa universe, I'd rather not do it. Based on the reactions and interpretations this post is getting, I'll probably just decide not to accept donations, and that's fine by me, lol.

Do you have any thoughts or input on what I'm saying?
